lines.label: PTAC exterior louver / architectural wall grille — material NOT settled (polypropylene kit vs aluminium architectural grille vs aluminium louver integral to the window system)

lines.instanceNote: NEEDS A RULING FROM AUSTIN ON SCOPE, and the argument is stated rather than decided. AGAINST keeping it on the room sheet: the louver is not visible, touchable or testable from inside the finished room — strictly it is an exterior elevation check, and the same arguable-call rule was applied to the fire damper, the volume damper and the gate valves but not here. FOR keeping it: it is this room's own PTAC assembly, nobody else's list is carrying it, and on floor 1 the exterior face is reachable at grade under this window in the same walk. Either rule it onto an exterior/facade punch with a cross-reference here, or keep it here — do not let it fall between the two. SEPARATELY, THE PRODUCT ITSELF IS FIVE STATEMENTS AND NO RESOLUTION: M201 = 'polypropylene louver kit (color by architect)'; M501 det.9 = 'aluminum architectural-style grille factory-painted to match exterior wall'; M401 KN1 = 'furnished with unit; grille painted to match exterior wall'; A200 keyed note 8 (= AS105 kn8) = 'ALUMINUM FIXED WINDOW … WITH INTEGRAL ALUMINUM LOUVER AT PTAC UNITS', i.e. part of the window system and the glazing sub's buy, not a PTAC accessory; AS103 corroborates the window-system reading. Polypropylene is moulded in colour and generally cannot be field-painted, so M201's product and M401's paint instruction may be physically incompatible. The size reference on A200/AS105 points to sheet A-601, which is NOT in the issued set (the set has A600 Doors and A610 Windows) — RFI R-04 — so the louver has no dimensional source either. SETTLES IT: one RFI to MWT / the M-EOR on material, finish, colour and which sub buys it, plus the A601-to-A610 correction.
